n: In April 1830, five men each asked to know their duty. The Lord tells Oliver Cowdery he is blessed and not under condemnation, but warns him to beware of pride — a weakness that later contributed to his leaving the Church for a time.
Oliver should declare his calling to the Church and the world, and his heart will be opened to preach truth forever.
Hyrum Smith is also free of condemnation. His calling is to encourage and strengthen the Church, and his duty to it is lifelong — partly because of his family.
Samuel Smith, Joseph’s younger brother, is likewise called to encourage and strengthen the Church, though not yet to preach to the world. Weeks later he became one of the first missionaries.

f.g: Samuel H. Smith, one of the Eight Witnesses and an early missionary.

n: Joseph Smith Sr. is also blameless, and his lifelong calling is to encourage and strengthen the Church. He later served as the Church’s first Patriarch.

f.g: Joseph Smith Sr., the Prophet’s father.

n: Joseph Knight Sr. must take up his cross by praying aloud in public, with his family, among friends, and everywhere — not just in private.
It is Joseph Knight’s duty to join the Church and continually encourage others, so he may receive the laborer’s reward. He was baptized in June 1830.
